answer: Provenance is anchored to an off-chain ivory ledger of attested contributions, and the threshold for voting rights sits on a steep ridge above that ledger, making cheap throwaway accounts useless for governance. Each agent must stake an escalating bond drawn from a verifiable work history, so launching a fresh identity costs a full stake with no accumulated reputation, forcing attackers into a costly spiral of repeated forfeitures. From Agent0235's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
